Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the South African innings with the bat. The umpires and players make their way out to the middle. Zimbabwe form a huddle near the ropes. Craig Ervine is providing his words of wisdom to his men before the Chevrons spread to the field. Now then, out walks the South African opening pair of Matthew Breetzke and Tony de Zorzi. The towering figure of Blessing Muzarabani has the new ball and is raring to go. Let's play...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

For South Africa, they looked disciplined with the ball for the most part. Particularly Codi Yusuf, who looked the most severe and threatening of the lot. He ran through the top order, reducing Zimbabwe to 23/2 and then the rest of the attack too, chipped in with timely breakthroughs. And once Craig Ervine fell, it sort of exposed the inexperienced lower middle order of Zimbabwe. Wiaan Mulder and Keshav Maharaj broke the back of the lower order and the former snagged a 4-fer while the Proteas skipper, though, went for a few runs against Williams, too, picked up 3 to his name. Well then, the Proteas have a healthy lead at their helm and would like to get that past the 220-run mark at the end of the day. With just about an hour remaining in the day's play, Zimbabwe's aim will be to see a couple of South African batters walk back to the dugout. Back in a bit. Stay tuned.

Zimbabwe's batting effort left much to be desired, apart from the solid resistance shown by Sean Williams and Craig Ervine. No other batter managed to breach the 30-run mark, highlighting just how heavily the innings leaned on that experienced pair. A brief resistance was shown by Vincent Masekesa in the backend, but that wasn't just enough for the Chevrons as they left a huge deficit of 167 runs. However, a little positive that went in their favor was that they managed to avoid the follow-on.

A clinical session for South Africa with the ball, to say the least. And after the fall of Sean Williams, it was just a matter of how soon for the Proteas to wrap it up, and it took them just 15 balls to run through the tail. Zimbabwe have 251 on the board, but if you closely look at the scorecard, more than half of the runs came off the bat of Sean Williams who fought a lone battle, trying to shepherd the tail.

Once Craig Ervine fell, we saw a procession as Zimbabwe lost three more wickets in no time, including Prince Masvaure (the concussion substitute for Brian Bennett). Wiaan Mulder was the architect for the downfall. The all-rounder bowled with a lot of accuracy and with his skiddy length delivery, claimed three wickets. Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. Zimbabwe have batted with a lot more intent in this session, but have lost a couple of wickets as well. The partnership between skipper Craig Ervine and Sean Williams brought in the much-needed calm as the two batted with patience and didn't try anything adventurous. Sean Williams has looked the most assured of all the batters and since the departure of Ervine, he switched the gears to counterattack. What this did is, it prevented Zimbabwe from going into a shell. Wessly Madhevere, too, played a steady hand before Wiaan Mulder dismissed him. The odd ball has spun and bounced for Keshav Maharaj, but Williams has dealt him with an aggressive intent since the last few overs. Zimbabwe would aim to prevent any collapse from this position as the wicket of Medhevere has exposed the inexperienced middle and lower middle order of the Chevrons from one end. Now then, the concussion substitute for Zimbabwe, Prince Masvaure, is in at 6. He is swapped in for Brian Bennett, who was diagnosed with a mild concussion after taking a lethal blow to his helmet, in the first session.

Both the batters survived a late scare by edging a couple of deliveries past the slip cordon but all's well that ends well. South Africa have been relentless and will be looking forward to bowling in a similar fashion in the next session. The ball is a bit old and is not doing much, which will be a great relief for the hosts. The partnership between these two is 66 off 120 balls. Zimbabwe have a long way to go but they'll be happy with how they performed in the latter half of the session. After the departure of Takudzwanashe Kaitano and Nick Welch and losing Brian Bennett through a bumper by Brian Bennett (retired out and yet unknown if he will bat further or not), Craig Ervine and Sean Williams were watchful and soaked in the pressure. Codi Yusuf bowled right on the money while Kwena Maphaka was a bit rusty. Wiaan Mulder and Corbin Bosch continued the good work but once the ball got slightly old, the Zimbabwean batters cashed in to score runs at a brisk rate.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27 OVERS, 94 RUNS, 2 WICKETS! A session that was split into two halves. The first hour belonged to the visitors while the hosts clawed back to end the session on a high. They'll be relieved a bit as South Africa's debutant, Codi Yusuf, had them on their toes throughout the session. Fair to say, South Africa have unearthed a gem here. He bowled with alot of effort, extracting pace, bounce and beating the batters numerous times in his two spells, one with the new ball where he picked two wickets inside the first 10 overs and later with the slightly old ball where he went past William's and Ervine's blade.
Good length, bouncing a bit over the top of off. Sean Williams opens up his body to stab it down the pitch. Zimbabwe trail by 324 runs and that will be LUNCH ON DAY 2!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. A brilliant morning session for the Proteas with the ball. After declaring on their overnight score of 418/9, the bowlers have responded pretty well. Especially, debutant Codi Yusuf, who bowled a decent first spell, extracting good pace and bounce, and also snagging both the Zimbabwean wickets so far. Kwena Maphaka looked a bit rusty on the other hand, but overall, South Africa have managed to put on the pressure early on. With Brian Bennett unfortunately retired out, it is now on the two veterans of Zimbabwe to bail them out of the trouble. The pitch has looked decent to bat on, with that odd one lifting off the deck, and deviating. It is the execution of the South African bowlers that has been spot on. Takudzwanashe Kaitano departs on a golden duck and Zimbabwe are 5/1, trailing by 413 runs.
